etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From French lampon (“satire, mockery, ridicule”), built on French lampons (“let us drink — a popular refrain for scurrilous songs”), from lamper (“to quaff, to swig”).
senses: A written attack or other work ridiculing a person, group, or institution; especially, a satirical one.
(transitive) To satirize or poke fun at.
